subject: DPA: segmented retention, onshore backup carveout, and erase handover
messages:
From: James Porter <jporter@acme-retail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 31 May 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA questions — retention buckets, onshore backup, and erase confirmation

Mina,

Thanks for taking this on. Our legal team attached a short list of asks in Acme_DPA_Requests_v1.pdf — high level: we need to confirm where production data will reside by region, an explicit backup retention window for onshore backups, and an SLA/process for certificate of deletion after a customer-initiated erase.

Two practical items we care about up front:
- Can Redwood commit to regional geofencing (US/EU) for customer production data and prevent cross-border backups except for explicit fallback?
- For backups/snapshots do you retain copies offsite or in a separate region and if so for how long? Acme policy prefers max 90 days unless a legal hold is in effect.

We anticipate procurement will need an official counter-redline for our DPA. Can you send suggested language and a short note about operational controls?

Thanks,
James Porter
Head of Security Operations
Acme Retail

Attachment: Acme_DPA_Requests_v1.pdf (PDF)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: James Porter <jporter@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 31 May 2028 11:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions — retention buckets, onshore backup, and erase confirmation

James —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick summary of what we can do and proposed redline language attached (Redwood_DPA_counter_redline.docx). High-level position:

1) Geofencing / residency
- We can geo-pin production tenant data to a chosen region (US/EU/APAC) and prevent automatic cross-region replication for primary dataset.
- We support a documented "geofallback" policy for capacity emergencies: Redwood may, in rare cases where capacity or availability is threatened, spin up temporary read-only replicas in a nearby region for up to 72 hours. This fallback is constrained by customer-configurable policies and must be logged and audited. Proposed clause included.

2) Backups / snapshots
- Backups are taken as incremental snapshots. Operationally we retain backups for 30 days by default.
- For customers requiring longer retention we propose an explicit addendum (tiered TTL). For onshore backups requested by procurement, we can agree to up to 90 days but will require a written justification and, if requested, an additional fee or reserved capacity commitment.

3) Erase / certificate of deletion
- Redwoods provides a Certificate of Deletion within 30 days of completion of the erase workflow for primary stores. For backups and immutable snapshots, we propose a 30–90 day purge window depending on the snapshot tier; certificate will note scope and timeline.

Operational controls notes (for procurement/security):
- SOC 2 Type II report available on request (link included in counter-redline).
- KMS controls: customer-managed keys available for dedicated/private deployments.
- Audit logs for any geofallback action and retained for 12 months.

I attached a counter-redline and a short "erase-playbook.md" we use internally to show step-by-step erasure handling. Karthik — can you add a short technical paragraph about snapshot lifecycle and the 30/90 day carveout?

Best,
Mina
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_counter_redline.docx (DOCX), erase-playbook.md (md)
From: James Porter <jporter@acme-retail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions — retention buckets, onshore backup, and erase confirmation

Mina —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from our counsel and procurement:

- Geofallback: 72 hours with audit sounds reasonable if it's truly limited, but we need a contractual guarantee that no persistent cross-border replica will be retained beyond that window without prior written consent.
- Onshore backup: Acme's procurement is prepared to accept the up-to-90-days carveout, but only if we get an explicit process around legal hold: who triggers it, how it's recorded, and how it overrides deletion windows.
- Certificate timing: 30 days for primary deletion is good. For backups, procurement wants the upper bound to be capped at 90 days and for the certificate to identify which snapshot tiers were in-scope.

Also — please send SOC2 evidence and any relevant KMS architecture docs to our security mailbox so we can run them past our reviewers.

If we can get a final DPA redline with the above clarifications, procurement will prepare a PO and we can loop in sales to finalize pricing.

James

Attachment: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: James Porter <jporter@acme-retail.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions — retention buckets, onshore backup, and erase confirmation

James —

Short technical clarifications and an implementation compromise that should satisfy procurement:

- Geofallback enforcement: We'll add explicit contract language that any temporary replica provisioned under the geofallback policy will be automatically destroyed after 72 hours and that destruction is verifiable via audit logs and snapshot digests. No persistent cross-border replica will be retained beyond 72 hours unless Acme provides written consent to extend.

- Legal hold process: Proposed flow — Acme sends a signed legal hold notification to legal@redwood.com with case id and scope (tenants, date ranges, affected artifacts). Redwood will respond with a hold acknowledgement within 48 hours and set a system-level flag that prevents automated purges for the affected artifacts. Holds will be logged and visible through our Console (audit trail). We will include this flow in the DPA as an appendix.

- Backups / snapshot tiers: Operationally we have three tiers: ephemeral (7 days), rolling (30 days), and long-tail (up to 90 days). For Acme's procurement we suggest defaulting to rolling (30 days) with an option to enable long-tail (90 days) via the DPA addendum. Certificates of Deletion will reference the tier identifiers and snapshot digests.

I attached a short excerpt from our erase-playbook.md showing the verification steps (hash checks, KMS key deletion events, audit log snapshot). If you want, Marissa can schedule a 30-minute runbook walk-through with your security team.

If Acme is comfortable with this, I can incorporate the language into the counter-redline and send a final version for signature.

-Karthik
Principal Architect, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachment: erase-playbook.md excerpt (text)

Karthik / Mina —

This reads well and answers the key procurement questions. Acme Legal is comfortable with:
- Geofallback automatic destroy after 72 hours, with audit verification language included.
- The legal hold flow (signed notice to legal@redwood.com, 48-hour ack, Console-visible flag).
- Backup tiers as described and Certificate of Deletion referencing snapshot tier and digests.

Procurement will accept the long-tail 90-day onshore backup option as an addendum linked to reserved capacity (we'll sign that as part of the PO). Please send the final DPA redline with the added geofallback clause, the legal-hold appendix, and the Certificate of Deletion template. If we get that over the next 48 hours we'll issue the PO and include the deal id below.

Thanks for the responsiveness — looking forward to closing this out.

James Porter
Head of Security Operations
